tools.name: software_search
tools.title: Search software
tools.description: Find software to install, as the Launcher's Install › Software does: apps (from Fedora's packages, source dnf, or Flathub, source flatpak; Fedora's first when both have it, Flathub's then in also) and command-line tools (dnf), each with name, summary, source, id and whether it's installed. One you can't install (the user's Access: Fedora's own repositories and Flathub's verified apps only, unless they allow more) has claude_can_install false and why: the user installs that one from the Launcher. Use software_info for one's details, software_preview before installing.

query.description: A name or what it does, e.g. 'gimp' or 'image editor'

tools.name: software_info
tools.title: Software details
tools.description: One package's, Flatpak app's or Nightdrive plugin's details: name, summary, whether it's installed, the description and fields (version, size, where it comes from, license, homepage; a plugin's needs and keys).

id.description: The package's name, the Flatpak app's id or the plugin's id, as software_search, software_installed or software_plugins give it

tools.name: software_installed
tools.title: Installed software
tools.description: What the user installed: the packages installed with dnf by name (not those that came along as dependencies, but also the system's own ones the installer chose) and the user's Flatpak apps, as the Launcher's Remove › Software lists them.

tools.name: software_plugins
tools.title: Nightdrive's plugins
tools.description: Nightdrive's optional parts (plugins, and apps such as Mail and Deck): id, name, description, group, whether each is installed and on, its version and where it comes from (Nightdrive, or an external plugin's repo). software_info with source plugin tells more of one.

tools.name: software_preview
tools.title: What installing or removing would do
tools.description: What installing or removing a package or Flatpak app would change, without changing anything: packages, the list of every package it would install, upgrade or remove ("name · repository"; with dnf, its dependencies, and for a removal the packages that need it), the disk space and, for a Flatpak app to install, its sandbox's permissions (permissions). When the user's Access doesn't let you make the change, it says so (claude_can_install or claude_can_remove false, and why): tell the user that instead of trying. Otherwise show the user this list, then give it as is to software_install or software_remove. Look closely at a removal's list: removing one package can take others the user needs along.

id.description: The package's name or the Flatpak app's id

tools.name: software_install
tools.title: Install software
tools.description: Install a package from Fedora's repositories (dnf) or an app from Flathub (flatpak, for this user), once the user allows it on Nightdrive's card, which shows where it comes from. Unless the user's Access allows more, every package of it must come from Fedora's own repositories (or Nightdrive's), and a Flathub app's publisher must be verified: anything else the user installs from the Launcher. packages must be software_preview's list as it gave it: if it no longer is what would be installed, nothing is. dnf then asks for the password in the system's own dialog (polkit): never ask the user for it yourself. Returns state installed, or running when a big download takes more than a few minutes (software_info tells when it's done).

id.title: Package
id.description: The package's name or the Flatpak app's id

tools.name: software_remove
tools.title: Remove software
tools.description: Remove a package (dnf) or one of the user's Flatpak apps, once the user allows it on Nightdrive's card. packages must be software_preview's list as it gave it, with everything that goes along: if it no longer is what would be removed, nothing is. dnf then asks for the password in the system's own dialog (polkit): never ask the user for it yourself. A Flatpak app's own data in ~/.var/app stays. Unless the user's Access allows it, nothing is removed whose list has a package Nightdrive installs (Hyprland, Quickshell, PipeWire, Firefox…): the desktop runs on them.

id.title: Package
id.description: The package's name or the Flatpak app's id

tools.name: software_plugin_install
tools.title: Install a Nightdrive plugin
tools.description: Install one of Nightdrive's plugins or apps (software_plugins), once the user allows it on Nightdrive's card: its installer opens in a terminal window, as from the Launcher's Install › Plugins, and asks the user there for what it needs (the password, tokens, choices); you wait until it's done. from must be where software_plugins says it comes from: Nightdrive, unless the user's Access lets you install other repositories' plugins too. Tell the user to look at the terminal window.

from.title: From
from.description: Where it comes from, as software_plugins gives it
